source_facts.fact: Farms remain subject to planning controls; changing land/buildings from farming to another use or building a house generally requires planning permission unless a specific right applies.
source_facts.gate: Agricultural ownership or use does not create a general development right.

source_facts.fact: The GOV.UK farm guidance states that farms of 5 hectares or more can benefit from specified agricultural permitted-development rights subject to conditions and possible prior approval.
source_facts.gate: PDR availability is not permission to ignore conditions or prior approval.

source_facts.fact: PPG states prior approval allows an LPA to consider only specified matters for the relevant PDR class.
source_facts.gate: Prior approval is not a full discretionary planning application.

source_facts.fact: Planning Data identifies Class Q as a permitted-development right for change of use of qualifying agricultural buildings to dwellinghouses plus reasonably necessary building operations.
source_facts.gate: Class Q category does not establish that a particular building qualifies.

source_facts.fact: PPG says qualifying farm-track works can use agricultural PDR but larger units can require prior approval.
source_facts.gate: A mapped farm track is not proof works are permitted.

source_facts.fact: 2026 farm accounts report diversification as non-agricultural entrepreneurial activity using farm resources and as a common farm-business strategy.
source_facts.gate: Economic diversification evidence is not planning permission for a proposed use.
